title: ITT and per-protocol estimands under treatment switching
text: many randomized trials treatment assigned baseline treatment received throughout follow-: control-arm patients cross experimental treatment, patients switch toxic regimens, others lost follow-. events happen continuous time recorded day, covariates drive (disease status, biomarkers) measured scheduled visits. Two estimands answer different questions, mapped ICH E9(R1) strategies: Treatment-policy (ITT): contrast randomized arms leaving switching naturally occurs (censoring removed). Hypothetical -switching (per-protocol, PP): contrast “assigned arm never switch” (switching censoring removed). vacttmle estimates exact switch dropout dates, adjusting visit-measured time-varying confounders drive switching dropout.

title: vacttmle 0.1.0
text: New primary functionality: treatment-switching estimands. va_ct_switch() estimates failure-free survival risk differences ICH E9(R1) treatment-policy (ITT) hypothetical -switching (per-protocol) strategies, using exact switch dropout dates visit-measured time-varying confounders. as_va_switch_data() builds analysis object tidy one-row-per- subject table plus subject--visit covariate matrix; simulate_va_switch_trial() generates example trials (scenarios A0–A7). Percentile weight control heavy switching via va_ct_switch(..., weight_trunc = "p95"), per-visit positivity diagnostics result object. Corrected efficient influence function: intervened switching censoring intensities enter cumulative inverse weight carry score terms; SEs calibrated (earlier internal formulation including coarsening “augmentation” scores passed mean-zero checks overstated variances — see paper’s gradient-pairing gate). Discrete-time LTMLE comparator (snap_to_grid(), est_discrete_ltmle()) explicit within-interval ordering conventions, reproducing paper’s ordering-sensitivity experiment. Composite-endpoint estimators retained 0.0.1. Note: composite path yet re-audited influence-function variance correction ; treat SEs potentially conservative.
